text_blocks.snippet: Treatment options for hypertension (high blood pressure) include a combination of healthy lifestyle changes and prescription medications.
snippet_highlighted_words: a combination of healthy lifestyle changes and prescription medications

list.snippet: DASH Diet: Eat a diet rich in fruits, vegetables, whole grains, and low-fat dairy while avoiding saturated fats.
Reduce Sodium: Limit salt intake to less than 2,300 milligrams (mg) per day, ideally aiming for under 1,500 mg.
Exercise Regularly: Engage in at least 30 minutes of moderate aerobic exercise, like brisk walking, most days of the week.
Lose Weight: Maintain a healthy weight; even a modest 5% weight loss can lower your numbers.
Limit Alcohol and Quit Smoking: Reduce alcohol consumption and avoid tobacco products completely.

text_blocks.snippet: If lifestyle changes are not enough, doctors prescribe first-line blood pressure medications, often starting with drugs listed by the American Heart Association:

list.snippet: ARBs (Angiotensin Receptor Blockers): Relax blood vessels by blocking a natural chemical that tightens them (e.g., losartan, valsartan).
ACE Inhibitors: Lower blood pressure by keeping blood vessels from narrowing (e.g., lisinopril, enalapril).
Calcium Channel Blockers: Prevent calcium from entering muscle cells in the heart and blood vessels to widen arteries (e.g., amlodipine).
Thiazide Diuretics ("Water Pills"): Help your body remove extra sodium and water through urine (e.g., hydrochlorothiazide).

text_blocks.snippet: You can read more detailed treatment guidelines on the Mayo Clinic High Blood Pressure Overview or the NIH High Blood Pressure Treatment Guide.
